title: Add Nsight Systems profile capture hook to benchmark runner (opt-in, case-scoped)
author: Isabella Rossi
description: Motivation: During the FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking sprint we’ve repeatedly hit “we need traces for these exact 2–3 cases” moments (TTFT regressions, unexpected variance, launch overhead vs memory-bound shifts). Today capturing Nsight Systems traces requires manual repro + bespoke commands, which slows down daily triage and makes it hard to correlate a trace with the exact harness config + artifact metadata. This PR adds an opt-in Nsight Systems capture hook to the benchmark runner so we can automatically collect and upload .nsys-rep traces for a small, explicit set of benchmark cases (shape/workload/model/GPU) without turning the whole matrix run into a profiling job. Overview of changes: (1) Adds runner flags to enable profiling and define which cases to profile: --profile.nsys=true|false (default false), --profile.nsys_cases=<path> (newline-delimited case IDs OR JSONL), --profile.nsys_max_captures=<N> (default 3), --profile.nsys_capture_prefill=true|false, --profile.nsys_capture_decode=true|false, --profile.nsys_timeout_s=<seconds> (default 180). (2) Wraps the actual benchmark invocation with `nsys profile` only when the case matches, and injects NVTX ranges around prefill/decode sections when available so the timeline is readable. (3) Uploads generated artifacts via the existing artifact uploader path (added in pr-19880) and writes a stable metadata sidecar: benchmark case ID, model identifier/hash, kernel_mode (baseline/fp8/int8), git SHA, CUDA/driver, GPU clocks setting, runner container digest, region/cluster, and command line. (4) Adds guardrails to avoid accidental massive uploads: hard cap on captures per run, max trace size threshold (default 2GB; above this we keep the metadata and log a warning but do not upload the trace), and automatic disabling when the runner detects it’s running under a shared fleet pool where profiling is forbidden (config-driven allowlist). (5) Documents how to view traces locally (nsys-ui) and how to find them in the benchmark artifact index (Console link + gs:// path printed in logs). Intended usage: For daily triage, drop a few suspect case IDs into a file (e.g., cases_to_profile.txt) and rerun the relevant slice of the matrix with --profile.nsys=true --profile.nsys_cases=cases_to_profile.txt. The runner will emit a summary table at the end with uploaded trace URIs and the matching case metadata, so kernel/scheduling folks can immediately open the right timeline. Notes: This is Nsight Systems (nsys) only (not Nsight Compute). Nsight Compute tends to require tighter control and can drastically perturb perf; we can add an analogous hook later behind an even stricter gate. The feature is no-op unless enabled; default behavior and benchmark outputs are unchanged. Testing: Added unit tests for case matching + command composition; added an integration smoke that runs a tiny synthetic “benchmark” process and verifies artifact upload wiring is invoked and metadata sidecar is written. Validated manually on an H100 run (single case) that the trace includes CUDA kernels and the NVTX prefill/decode ranges. Risk/impact: Minimal for normal benchmarking because the hook is off by default. When enabled, profiling overhead is expected (and desired) for those few cases; we log prominently and annotate the results as “profiled” so they are not used for perf aggregates. This is aligned with sprint workflow: keep matrix runs clean, but allow targeted trace capture when needed.

review_conversation: Rina Kobayashi: Can we make sure profiled runs never get mixed into aggregate metrics? I don’t want someone to accidentally publish a “perf regression” that is just profiling overhead. Isabella Rossi: Yep—added a `profiled=true` tag in the result JSON and the aggregator now excludes any run with that tag by default; also prints a warning block in stdout when profiling is enabled. Grace Kim: Please add an explicit cap and size guard; I’ve seen nsys-rep files explode on long decode traces. Isabella Rossi: Added `--profile.nsys_max_captures` (default 3) and `--profile.nsys_max_size_gb` (default 2). If the trace exceeds the cap, we keep metadata + logs and skip upload. Noah Patel: How are we ensuring the trace is linked back to the exact kernel mode + git SHA? We’ve had confusion in the past. Isabella Rossi: Sidecar metadata includes git SHA, kernel_mode, model hash, CUDA/driver, container digest, clocks pinned flag, and case ID. The artifact uploader also records those fields for search. Julian Moore: NVTX ranges: are these always on? Any runtime overhead? Isabella Rossi: NVTX compile is guarded; at runtime it’s enabled only when profiling is enabled in the runner (env var), otherwise it’s a no-op. Also added minimal ranges: prefill/decode boundaries + scheduler tick. Rina Kobayashi (request changes): Please update docs with exact commands and note that profiled results are excluded. Isabella Rossi: Done. Rina Kobayashi: LGTM. Grace Kim: Approved. Noah Patel: Approved.
release_notes: Internal: Benchmark runner supports opt-in Nsight Systems trace capture for selected cases; traces are uploaded with metadata sidecars and excluded from perf aggregates by default.
